description: "Get this fix": a site fix served finished, with paste steps for the platform the site runs on: the business-facts structured data and the llms.txt are written from the facts its owner confirmed; the robots.txt lines from what the newest audit found blocked. Use this when someone asks to "get this fix," "do it for me," "give me the structured data / llms.txt / robots.txt lines to paste," or wants a fix done rather than described. Returns status "served" with the request (its `id` is what check_fix checks) and the fix: each block ready to copy, the steps for the site's platform (or the `platform` given), and `copy_all`, the prompt and every block in one paste, where the steps carry a prompt for the agent that edits the site. Each call is recorded as a request for the fix. When the newest audit found nothing for the fix to change (for robots_txt, no AI assistant blocked), it returns status "nothing_to_fix" and records nothing. Nothing that states the owner's facts is served before the owner has confirmed them: then it returns status "confirm_first" with the `reason`, the confirm block and `seen` — show the owner those facts, and once they confirm or correct them, call confirm_facts with `seen` unchanged and ask again. With reason "facts_not_read" the site has not been read yet, so there is nothing to confirm until its next weekly check. It answers only for a site the account tracks. Requires a Website Auditor subscription ($49/month; eligible new customers get a 7-day free trial — payment method required, no charge until the trial ends) — if the user doesn't have one, call get_sample_audit first to show them the exact output format, free and with no API key.

kind.description: Which fix: "business_facts" (structured data plus About and FAQ text, from the owner's confirmed facts), "llms_txt" (an llms.txt titled with the confirmed name), or "robots_txt" (Allow lines for the AI assistants the newest audit found blocked by robots.txt; it states no facts, so nothing is confirmed first). Left out, the site's top fix.

platform.description: The platform to write the steps for, one of the `platforms` keys in the site's fix list (e.g. "wordpress", "shopify", "developer_host"). Left out, the platform detected for the site.

name: get_fix

confirm.description: The confirm block: each fact with what the site says and what the owner confirmed.

can_confirm.description: False when the site has not been read, so nothing can be confirmed yet.

confirmed.description: What the owner confirmed, or null.

site.description: What the site says for this fact.

stale.description: True when the site changed this fact since the owner confirmed it.

content.description: Ready to copy as it is.

checks.description: What a live check reads to say the fix is live.

copy_all.description: The agent prompt and every block in one paste; null where the steps carry no prompt.

facts.description: The confirmed facts the fix states.

agent_prompt.description: A prompt for the agent that edits the site, where the platform has one.

reason.description: Present on confirm_first: "unconfirmed", "stale" (the site changed a confirmed fact), "no_name", or "facts_not_read" (the site has not been read, so nothing can be confirmed yet).

request.description: Present when served: the request this call was recorded as.

id.description: The request's id: what a live check of this fix takes.

path.description: How it was asked for: "served" (the dashboard), "mcp" or "api".

status.description: "live", "missing", or null before a check reached the site.

seen.description: Present on confirm_first when the owner can answer it.

status.description: "served": the fix, finished. "confirm_first": nothing served; the facts it states are not confirmed by the owner yet. "nothing_to_fix": nothing served; the site's newest audit found nothing for this fix to change.

title: Get this fix
